questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

Rajib’s grandfather (a)/ asked him to (b)/buy a dozen egg (c)/ from the market (d)/ No error
questions.explanation:
• Countable nouns are those nouns that you can count.
  • Countable nouns have singular and plural forms.
    • Examples: Ball, egg, boy, cat, person, etc.
  • Here, the word dozen refers to twelve pieces of eggs. Hence, the singular noun ‘egg’ has been wrongly used in place of ‘eggs’.

Therefore, the correct answer is option C.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, a sentence has been divided into four parts, one of which may contain an error. Identify that part and mark it as your answer. If the given sentence is correct as it is, mark ‘No Error’ as the answer. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.

Karim has successfully(A)/ completed a four–years degree(B)/ course from(C)/ Narula Institute of Technology.(D)/No error
questions.explanation:
• The error is in part B of the sentence. The error is related to the use of the singular form after a numeral when used as a compound adjective. 
  • When expressions of measurement, time, age, distance, or quantity are used as compound adjectives before a noun, the singular form of the noun is used, not plural.
  • Example: He bought a two-kilometer-long rope.
  • In the sentence, "four–years degree" is incorrect because "four-year" is acting as a compound adjective describing the noun "degree". So, "year" should be singular.
  • “four-year” is a compound adjective because it combines a number and a noun to describe another noun “degree course”. In such cases, the noun stays singular and is usually hyphenated.
  • Corrected Sentence:
    Karim has successfully completed a four-year degree course from Narula Institute of Technology
  • Therefore, the correct answer is option D.

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

The villagers mentioned (a)/ in their tales that(b)/ many a kids were (c)/drowned in the river.(d)/No error
questions.explanation:
• The phrase "many a" is always followed by a singular noun/ pronoun/ verb.
  • Here, the noun should be singular, and so should the verb.
  • Here, we need to use ‘kid’ instead of ‘kids’ and ‘was’ in place of ‘were’.

Therefore, the correct answer is option c.

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

Owing to his busy life, (A)/ he could not write even the two-third (B)/ of the book, which (C)/the publication was expected to release before January. (D)/ No Error (E)
questions.explanation:
The erroneous part of the sentence is (B). 

The phrase "the two-third" is incorrect; it should be written as "two-thirds". When referring to a fraction or proportion that is more than one unit, the ordinal number part (the denominator) is typically pluralized.

This is a noun-based fraction error.
Rule:
Fractions greater than one are written in plural form.

Hence, option B is the correct choice.

Corrected sentence:

Owing to his busy life, he could not write even two-thirds of the book, which the publication was expected to release before January.

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

Mr Sagar has now (a)/got a whole week(b)/ to himself and(c)/ he can read to his heart’s contents.(d)/ No error
questions.explanation:
• There is an error in part d of the given sentence.
  • The meaning of certain nouns in the plural form is quite different from their meaning in the singular form.
  • The word ‘content’ is one such word. Here in the given sentence, the word ‘content’ means “a state of satisfaction”.
  • On the other hand, the word, ‘contents’ means ‘the things that are held or included in something’.
  • Here, the state of being satisfied is clearly mentioned.
  • Thus, we should use ‘heart’s content’ to make the given sentence grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is option c.

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

You can barely walk because your toes are (A)/ pinched, ugh. This footwear just doesn’t fit; (B)/ as in the new novel, “Someone’s Else Shoes” by Jojo Moyes, (C)/ you can’t wait to kick things off. (D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation:
• The error lies in part (c) of the sentence.
    When forming the possessive of phrases like “someone else”, the apostrophe-s (’s) is added to the word “else,” not “someone.”
  • The phrase “someone else” is a compound indefinite pronoun where "else" is part of the unit. To show possession (shoes that belong to someone else), you need to add the apostrophe-s to the entire phrase, i.e., at the end — else’s.

    Corrected Sentence:
    You can barely walk because your toes are (A)/ pinched, ugh. This footwear just doesn’t fit; (B)/ as in the new novel, “Someone Else’s Shoes” by Jojo Moyes, (C)/ you can’t wait to kick things off. (D)/ No error (E)

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

The courage of the Romans, however, soon (A)/ overcame such fears; the Britons were put to (B)/ flight; and the groves of Mona, the scene of many (C)/ a sacrifices and bloody rite, were cut down. (D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation:
Correct Sentence:
The courage of the Romans, however, soon overcame such fears; the Britons were put to flight; and the groves of Mona, the scene of many a sacrifice and bloody rite, were cut down.

Explanation:
The determiner "many a" is always followed by a singular countable noun, not a plural noun. Therefore, "many a sacrifices" should be "many a sacrifice."

Rule :
Many + Plural Noun → many sacrifices
Many a + Singular Noun → many a sacrifice

questions.question:
Directions: In the following question, a sentence has been divided into four parts, one of which may contain an error. Identify the part that contains the error and mark it as your answer. If the sentence is correct as it is, choose 'No Error' as your answer. Ignore errors in punctuation, if any. 

Since there is a little(a)/ milk left in the jar, (b) /you cannot make three (c)/ cups of tea with it. (d)/ No error
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: Option A (a)

  • The error lies in part (a): "Since there is a little."
  • The sentence states, "...you cannot make three cups of tea with it," which implies that there is almost no milk, or an insufficient amount of milk. 
    "A little" means a small amount but some (positive connotation, implying there is enough to use).
    "Little" means hardly any (negative connotation, implying there is not enough). 
    Since the context implies the amount is insufficient, "a little" should be replaced with "little". 

Corrected Sentence: Since there is little milk left in the jar, you cannot make three cups of tea with it.

Direction: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

questions.explanation:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is A, "Raghavendra is a fifty years old".  

  • If we use a noun to describe another noun that is called a noun modifier. It cannot be used in plural form.
  • In the given sentence ‘years’ is used as a noun modifier to describe ‘Man’.
  • Therefore, the singular form ‘year’ must be used in place of ‘years’.

Correct sentence: Raghavendra is a fifty-year-old man and he loves his family including two daughters and one son.

Hence, the correct answer is "Raghavendra is a fifty years old".

questions.question:
Direction: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error mark (E) as your answer choice. 

All these changes happening around us will certainly cause a great harm to our environment.
questions.explanation:
The sentence is grammatically incorrect and the error lies in "cause a great harm". The error is related to the Noun.

  • A few nouns like Advice, Information, Furniture, Luggage, Baggage, Knowledge, Brokerage, Postage, Scenery, Poetry, Stationary, Crockery, Jewelry, Harm, Damage, Health, Equipment, Evidence, Mischief, Hair, Alphabet, Work, Paper, Money, Traffic, Food, Fruit, Fuel, Death, Life, Time, etc. are considered uncountable nouns.
    • Uncountable nouns always take singular verbs according to them if they are used as subjects.
    • Uncountable nouns never take (a/an) articles with them.
    • Uncountable nouns don't have plural forms.
  • In the given sentence ‘harm’ is used in the C part which is an uncountable noun and cannot take (a/an) article with it.
  • Thus, "cause great harm to our environment" must be used in place of "cause a great harm to our environment".

Correct sentence: All these changes happening around us will certainly cause great harm to our environment.

Hence, the correct answer is "cause a great harm".

questions.question:
Direction: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then mark (E) as the correct answer choice. 

There is no money left in John’s and Helen’s joint account at present, as the entire balance has already been used.
options: left in John’s and Helen’s joint account
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option B.

When possessive nouns are joined together, we add the apostrophe to the last name only. Also, they agree with a plural verb.
For example, Ronaldo and Messi’s records are quite hard to break.

Similarly, in this question, John and Helen are two possessive nouns.
The apostrophe (’s) should be added to the last name only.

Therefore, the apostrophe (’s) should be removed from “John” to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Corrected sentence is as follows:

There is no money left in John and Helen’s joint account at present, as the entire balance has already been used.

Hence, option B is the correct choice.

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

According to the report by the United Nations(a)/ regarding the most generous (b)/woman in the world, Mrs Catherine(c)/ is better than any woman. (d)/No error
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Part D — "is better than any woman"
Part D is erroneous due to the incorrect comparative structure, which should be replaced with "is better than any other woman."
The sentence is saying that Mrs Catherine is the most generous woman in the world. But when we use a comparative degree like "better than" to express that someone is superior to all others in a group, we must always add the word "other" to exclude the person being compared from the group itself.
"Is better than any woman" is wrong because Mrs Catherine herself is also a woman. So technically the sentence is saying she is better than herself too, which is logically impossible. Adding "other" fixes this by saying she is better than every other woman — excluding herself from the comparison.

The correct sentence would be — According to the report by the United Nations regarding the most generous woman in the world, Mrs Catherine is better than any other woman.

Additional Information
Comparative + "other" rule: whenever a subject is being compared with a group it belongs to using comparative degree, "other" must always be added to exclude the subject from that group. Without "other" the subject ends up being compared with itself which is logically impossible 

For Example — Sachin is better than any other cricketer in the team. / This building is taller than any other building in the city.

Superlative vs Comparative for same meaning: both structures can express the same idea but with different grammar. "She is the most generous woman" uses superlative correctly. "She is more generous than any other woman" uses comparative correctly. Both are right. But "more generous than any woman" without "other" is always wrong.

For Example — He is the fastest runner. / He is faster than any other runner. Both correct. "Faster than any runner" without other will be wrong.

questions.question:

Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.

Death had been far from co-dependent, and he'd had free rein until two days ago, (B)/ when he crossed into the underworld with Katie slung across his shoulder. (C)/ He'd forgotten what it was to have someone completely dependent on him. (D)
questions.explanation:
Explanation:

The noun "human world" is a specific noun phrase and requires the definite article "the" when paired with another definite place (the underworld).

Correct parallel structure:

the underworld
the human world

Omitting "the" before "human world" breaks the parallelism and makes the expression grammatically incomplete.

Correct Sentence:

He'd spent his life relatively alone, crossing between the underworld and the human world as needed. Death had been far from co-dependent, and he'd had free rein until two days ago, when he crossed into the underworld with Katie slung across his shoulder. He'd forgotten what it was to have someone completely dependent on him.
